newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's PDVSA sees six mln bpd output in 2005.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's PDVSA sees six mln bpd output in 2005.

text.p: Venezuela's state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) said it sees its crude output capacity rising to six million barrels per day in 2005 from 3.179 million bpd in 1995, PDVSA Vice-President Claus Graf said.
He told reporters that PDVSA also planned to increase its 1995-2005 investment program to between $68 and $70 billion from $65 billion.
"These are the latest figures we're using," he said.
Speaking after a press conference to present PDVSA's third marginal field auctions, Graf said the investment figures were revised periodically, the last time in October.

He gave no details but PDVSA said earlier the investment plan included at least $11 billion under the profit sharing scheme for exploration and production of 10 fields that was put in motion last January, the so-called oil opening.
Revitalization of old fields forms part of Venezuela's plans to boost crude oil output to over six million bpd in the next 10 years.
Industry sources said Venezuela is currently producing well above its OPEC quota output of 2.359 million bpd and that production in recent months was consistently over three million bpd.
